results.title: ‘Some people are suffering, GH¢700 a month is unjustifiable’ — NAGRAT president
results.content: The President of the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT), Jacob Anaba, has described the monthly earnings of some public sector workers as unjustifiable, saying members of his association are struggling to make ends meet despite the annual salary adjustments.

results.title: Bawumia explores Japan’s AI and satellite technology applications during study tour
results.content: New Patriotic Party (NPP) 2028 flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia has visited leading Japanese research institutions and technology firms as part of a study tour focused on how advanced scientific research can be applied to address practical development challenges.

results.title: Bronx residents plan vigil for slain Ghanaian teenager amid calls to tackle youth violence
results.content: Residents of the Bronx neighbourhood in New York where 15-year-old Ghanaian teenager Javits Badu Nkansah Frimpong was shot dead are planning a vigil to honour him and demand action against rising youth violence.

results.title: 8% pay rise: ‘We are not being paid realistic salaries’— PSWU
results.content: The eight per cent increase in base pay for public sector workers in 2027 will not address what the Public Services Workers’ Union (PSWU) describes as the fundamental problem of unrealistic salaries in the public service.

results.title: NIA develops mobile app to extend Ghana Card biometric verification to individuals, small businesses
results.content: The National Identification Authority (NIA) is preparing to introduce a mobile application that will allow individuals and small businesses to verify identities through the Ghana Card biometric system without having to access its main verification platform.

results.title: Free SHS food suppliers threaten five-day protest over unpaid 2024 debts
results.content: The Controlled Food Suppliers Association (CFSA) has announced plans to embark on a five-day demonstration at the Ghana Commodity Exchange (GCX) in Accra over outstanding payments for food items supplied under the Free Senior High School (Free SHS) programme in 2024.

results.title: Gov’t targets illegal mining, not the mining industry – Mahama Ayariga
results.content: The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, clarified that the government’s campaign against galamsey is not meant to abolish mining but to eliminate activities outside the country’s legal framework.

results.title: GPCL reforms operations to boost growth
results.content: The Ghana Publishing Company Limited (GPCL) is restructuring its operations to expand its West African market presence and improve commercial performance.

results.title: GAC raises concern over declining condom use, HIV stigma
results.content: The Ghana AIDS Commission (GAC) says declining condom use among adults engaging in higher-risk sex and persistent discrimination against people living with HIV are threatening Ghana’s efforts to control the epidemic.

results.title: UCC inaugurates centre to tackle food fraud in Africa
results.content: The University of Cape Coast (UCC) has inaugurated the Africa Centre for Food Integrity (AFIC) to address food safety and quality challenges in Ghana and Africa.

results.title: Here’s what to expect from the ‘New Economy’ in the 2027 Budget
results.content: Government plans to invest approximately $10 billion over four years in what it calls a “New Economy”, with agriculture, manufacturing and job creation at the centre of the programme. A Finance Ministry document has provided an early indication of what to expect when Finance Minister Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson presents the budget on November 12. […]

results.title: No new Ghana Cards required under biometric verification law – NIA
results.content: The National Identification Authority (NIA) has assured Ghanaians that the implementation of the National Identity Register Amendment Regulation, 2026 (L.I. 2523), does not require the acquisition of new Ghana Cards or undergoing fresh biometric registration.

results.title: Ghana envoy expects US police to identify killers of teenager shot dead in New York
results.content: Ghana’s Ambassador to the United States, Victor Emmanuel Smith, says he expects American investigators to make progress in identifying those behind the fatal shooting of 15-year-old Ghanaian teenager Javits Badu Nkansah Frimpong in New York.

results.title: Queen Máxima in Ghana to push financial security as only 22% of adults are financially healthy
results.content: From the evening of Monday 2nd November until Thursday 5 November, Her Majesty Queen Máxima will visit the Republic of Ghana in her capacity as the United Nations Secretary-General’s Special Advocate for Financial Health (UNSGSA). She will speak with people who use financial services, as well as with representatives of government, development organisations and financial institutions, about policies and services that contribute to the financial resilience and the wellbeing of Ghana’s people.

results.title: ‎Bawumia calls for laws to protect workers from AI job losses
results.content: Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, Flagbearer of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), has called for legislation to protect workers from potential job losses arising from the growing use of Artificial Intelligence (AI).

results.title: Mahama appoints Dr Hamid Kanyiti Salifu as Acting Deputy CEO of Student Loan Trust Fund
results.content: President John Mahama has appointed Dr Hamid Kanyiti Salifu as Acting Deputy Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Student Loan Trust Fund (SLTF) to strengthen the institution’s leadership and efforts to improve access to tertiary education financing.

results.title: Illegal mining threatening Ghana’s relations with neighbouring countries – Zanetor
results.content: The escalating illegal mining activities in Ghana are threatening the diplomatic relations between the country and its immediate neighbours in the West Africa sub-region.

results.title: Ghana Reference Rate falls to 10.01%, signalling further relief for borrowers
results.content: The Ghana Reference Rate (GRR), a key benchmark commercial banks use to price loans, has fallen to 10.01% for November 2026, signalling potential relief for borrowers.

results.title: Afenyo-Markin calls for stronger enforcement of audit findings across Africa
results.content: Alexander Afenyo-Markin, the Minority Leader in Parliament, has called on African countries to move beyond merely identifying financial irregularities and ensure the effective enforcement of audit recommendations to strengthen public accountability.

results.title: Without the media, there is no democracy – Major (rtd) Don-Chebe
results.content: Major (rtd) Albert Don-Chebe, former Director-General of the Ghana Broadcasting Corporation (GBC), has described the media as the foundation of democracy because it safeguards and promotes democratic governance and accountability.

results.title: Richmond Adu-Poku: Too many shows, too little December
results.content: The audience cannot be in two places at once. The wallet cannot be stretched indefinitely. And the calendar, unfortunately, has refused to add extra days simply because our favourite artistes want to headline.

results.title: Cape Coast Court Complex falls silent as JUSAG strike locks out litigants
results.content: An unusual, deafening silence hung over the Cape Coast Court Complex on Monday, as the Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG) nationwide strike brought judicial activities in the Central Regional capital to a standstill.

results.title: Mahama Ayariga warns MMDCEs, Regional Ministers against turning blind eye to galamsey
results.content: The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, has warned Regional Ministers and Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs) that they cannot escape responsibility for illegal mining under their watch.

results.title: The Multimedia Group tops 30th GJA Media Awards with nine nominations
results.content: The Multimedia Group has topped nominations for the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards, securing nine nominations across its subsidiaries ahead of the awards ceremony on Saturday, November 7, 2026.

results.title: TRAFFITEC-GH: The good, the bad and what could be
results.content: TRAFFITEC-GH has the potential to improve road safety, but its success depends on effective execution, public education, sound infrastructure and institutional accountability. Political loyalty should never replace objective scrutiny, just as opposition should not dismiss a potentially beneficial initiative.

results.title: Traffitech: Katanomics can turn smart ideas into absurdities
results.content: Traffitech-GH went live on 1 November.

results.title: Housing deficit falls to 1.8 million, but service gaps remain — GSS
results.content: Ghana’s estimated housing deficit declined from 2.8 million units in 2010 to 1.8 million in 2021, but persistent gaps in access to electricity, sanitation and decent settlement conditions continue to affect households across the country.

results.title: Three in 10 urban residents live in slums, informal settlements — GSS
results.content: Nearly one in three people living in Ghana’s urban areas resides in a slum or informal settlement, highlighting the housing and basic-service challenges accompanying the country’s rapid urbanisation.

results.title: Ghana’s inflation projected to stay below 10% for next three to four years – Theo Acheampong
results.content: Economist and political risk specialist Dr Theo Acheampong says Ghana’s inflation is projected to remain below 10 per cent over the next three to four years.

results.title: Ghana’s urban population hits 19.8 million as housing, sanitation gaps persist
results.content: Nearly 19.8 million people, representing 58.7 per cent of Ghana’s population, lived in urban areas in 2025, putting renewed focus on the country’s growing demand for housing, sanitation and other essential services.
